title: Touchscreen MacBook Pro hands-on: OLED looks great on a Mac
gist: In a brief hands-on, Ars found the touchscreen MacBook Pro's OLED display an enormous upgrade over MiniLED, but the touchscreen adds little beyond trackpad gestures and lacks Apple Pencil or tablet mode. Price is the barrier: a 16-inch M5 Max with 64GB/2TB costs $5,799, and the 128GB RAM upgrade adds $1,600.

insights.claim: The MacBook Pro touchscreen works as expected, but there is not much you can do with it at the OS level that trackpad gestures couldn't already do, though some creative apps offer more.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: The touchscreen is unlikely to be a major upgrade driver by itself.
insights.quote: there’s not much you can do with it that you couldn’t already do with trackpad gestures, at least at the OS level
